scope: English Year 3 — 14 source-task objectives absent from existing standalone header

62.excerpt: Groups gather facts, write short descriptions of a country's weather, activities and features
62.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can write short descriptions of a selected country's weather, activities and features for a country collage and request help appropriately.

74.excerpt: Pupils retell two events from the story and give one personal response.
74.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can retell two events from 'We're Going Home' and give one personal response to the story.

108.excerpt: Teacher listens to each pupil asking and answering one question about time and one about a place.
108.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can ask and answer one question about time and one about a place using short, clear sentences.

111.excerpt: Teacher asks each pupil to name a favourite scene and explain why, using one detail from the story.
111.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can name a favourite scene from 'The Secret Tunnel' and explain why, using one supporting story detail.

114.excerpt: Teacher listens to each pupil recount one place visited yesterday and make one polite request for help or clarification.
114.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can describe one place they visited yesterday and make one polite request for help or clarification.

119.excerpt: Teacher observes each pupil giving a short account of a past visit and answering one partner question about the experience.
119.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can give a short account of a past visit and answer one partner question about that experience.

121.excerpt: Pairs complete the comparison table and write at least two sentences about their hometown in the past
121.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can write at least two sentences comparing their hometown in the past and present while checking apostrophes, spelling and punctuation.

139.excerpt: Listeners sketch the six events, including negative events
139.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can listen to a six-event holiday story, sketch the six events and explain one event they heard.

141.excerpt: Teacher asks pupils to locate two answers in James's email and identify one example of correct email punctuation.
141.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can locate two answers in James's holiday email and identify one example of correct email punctuation.

144.excerpt: Teacher checks two present/past verb pairs and one written past-tense sentence per pupil
144.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can produce two present/past verb pairs and one accurate written past-tense sentence.

148.excerpt: Pairs write at least two descriptive sentences about one endangered animal, using comparatives where appropriate.
148.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can write at least two descriptive sentences about an endangered Malaysian animal, using relevant comparisons and checking spelling.

149.excerpt: Pairs select two animals, write two clue sentences for each and practise singing or miming their clues.
149.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can write two animal clue sentences for each of two animals, including facts and comparisons, and present their clues.

157.excerpt: Read and sequence four original model-making instructions, then locate two details.
157.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can read and sequence four Solar System model-making instructions and locate two details.

158.excerpt: Teacher checks two planet descriptions and the poster labels.
158.objective: By the end of the lesson, pupils can write two planet descriptions for a labelled imaginary Solar System poster and correct a spelling error after feedback.
